neighboring_unit_entries.title: Incipient-horizon rescaling produces an L^-5 contribution and critical summability threshold
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: At touching radius, each incipient coordinate plane contains horizons indexed by all primitive lattice vectors. Rescaling the two-dimensional transverse gap yields a universal four-parabola region; its visibility integral is numerically estimated and gives FH(t) proportional to t^-2 L^-5. Summing indices becomes an Epstein series convergent through dimension five and divergent from six.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Velocity correlations are compared directly with free-flight predictions
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The source tests Conjecture 3 by fitting velocity autocorrelation to C_r/t and comparing C_r with the horizon-sum limit of tF(t) across scatterer radii. This is the empirical bridge from collision-free geometry to diffusion.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: At the touching transition, countably many subordinate horizons contribute with L^-5 weights; their lattice sum changes from convergent to divergent at dimension six, providing a mechanism for a critical decay law.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Divergence proves neither the logarithm at d=6 nor the fractional exponents above it; those remain conjectural and numerically supported.
